stories.title: Temporal transcriptomic and physiological analyses reveal salinity-dependent adaptation in Tripolium pannonicum
stories.description: Tripolium pannonicum, a salt-tolerant halophyte, is a useful system for investigating plant responses to salinity. Here, we integrated physiological measurements with transcriptome profiling across six NaCl concentrations (0–16‰) and multiple time points. Based on growth responses, treatments were classified as low (3‰ and 6‰), moderate (8‰), or high (12‰ and 16‰) salinity. Salt exposure altered osmotic adjustment and antioxidant-enzyme activities in concentration- and time-dependent manners. Under low salinity, soluble osmolyte contents and antioxidant-enzyme activities changed gradually and remained comparatively stable. Moderate salinity produced a transient increase in soluble protein and sustained peroxidase activity. High salinity induced early osmolyte accumulation and a rapid increase in catalase activity at 0.5 h, followed by declining antioxidant-enzyme activities during prolonged exposure. Transcriptome analysis revealed salinity-dependent gene-expression responses, with differentially expressed genes enriched in MAPK signalling, plant hormone signal transduction, phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, and flavonoid biosynthesis. Temporal clustering identified early, intermediate, and late response patterns associated with hormone-related signalling, metabolic adjustment and genome maintenance, and transcriptional adaptation, respectively. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified modules correlated with soluble sugar content and catalase activity. Together, these results provide a time-resolved description of physiological and transcriptional responses to salinity in T. pannonicum and nominate candidate pathways for functional validation.
